title: Scan-time replacement can authorize an outside-scope file under a benign name
confidence: high (0.91) in the code interleaving; medium in practical race reliability
summary: During a non-preview `kcs index`, the scanner checks that a selected-scope direct child is a regular file and derives policy from its benign relative name, but later follows the mutable pathname to compute the accepted scan hash. A lower-trust directory writer who replaces that child with a symlink after the type check can make KCS bind outside victim-readable bytes to the benign in-scope identity; later hash equality accepts the same outside target because the scan hash was already computed from it.

codeEvidence.label: Non-preview index requests raw hashes during scan
codeEvidence.explanation: A normal non-preview `index` call asks the scanner to include a `raw_hash`, so the scan-stage file identity becomes an input to the later indexing pipeline.

codeEvidence.label: Scanner observes the direct child as a regular file
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker-controlled directory entry is accepted because it is observed as a regular direct child at this moment. The result is not bound to an open descriptor, so a later rename can change what `path` resolves to.

codeEvidence.label: Benign-name policy precedes a following pathname read
codeEvidence.explanation: `relative` drives the secret decision, but `std::fs::read(&path)` follows the current pathname. A replacement symlink can therefore supply outside bytes while retaining the benign in-scope name and policy result.

codeEvidence.label: Later hash equality accepts the same outside target
codeEvidence.explanation: The hash check catches ordinary post-scan edits, but not this interleaving: `candidate.raw_hash` and `current_hash` can both be the outside target's hash. The secret hold still uses `candidate.input_path`, and only the mutable path is passed onward.

codeEvidence.label: Preparation independently reopens the input path
codeEvidence.explanation: `prepare_units()` receives `raw_hash` but does not consume the previously verified buffer. It opens `request.input_path` again, preserving the pathname-binding weakness into preparation.

codeEvidence.label: OCR client reopens the path before sending
codeEvidence.explanation: When the ordinary online OCR path is otherwise authorized, the adapter performs a final pathname read and serializes those bytes into the request body. No descriptor or byte-buffer binding from scan time reaches this sink.

codeEvidence.label: Embedding secret hold uses stored raw path
codeEvidence.explanation: Derived content later relies on the stored raw path for secret holds. If outside content was adopted under a benign raw path, this downstream control sees the benign identity rather than the physical target.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that direct-child authorization, secret/media decisions, raw hashing, preparation, and online sends must describe the same file identity. KCS observes the initial directory entry as a regular file but then relies on repeated pathname reads; a replacement symlink can make the accepted hash and later bytes come from outside the selected scope while policy remains tied to the benign relative name.

validation.method: static source trace plus local/offline synthetic PoC
validation.summary: The source trace confirms the multi-stage interleaving: the scanner checks a regular direct child, classifies the benign relative name, computes the scan hash through a later path read, and the index pipeline accepts a reread when it equals that already-substituted hash. The included PoC deterministically models this state transition with synthetic files.
assertions: A symlink present at the initial type check is skipped, but a later replacement is not bound to the earlier regular-file observation.
The later `candidate.raw_hash` comparison does not reject this case because the scan hash can already be the outside target's hash.
Preparation and OCR continue to receive or read a mutable path rather than the scan-verified byte buffer.
limitations: No live KCS timing race was executed.
Race reliability and an end-to-end OCR request capture were not measured.
The PoC uses synthetic local files and does not access real private data or any live service.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust writer places a benign regular file in a selected scope, replaces it with a symlink after KCS observes the regular file, and leaves the link pointed at a victim-readable outside target. KCS hashes and later rereads that outside target while retaining the benign in-scope identity.

dataflow.summary: benign direct-child path -> `entry.file_type()` regular observation -> benign `relative` policy -> following `std::fs::read(&path)` scan hash -> later equal index reread -> preparation/OCR path reopens
dataflow.source: concurrent replacement of a selected-scope direct child by a lower-trust directory writer
dataflow.sink: prepared/local KCS state under the benign raw path and, when separately authorized, Mistral OCR request bytes
dataflow.outcome: outside victim-readable bytes can be adopted or sent under a benign in-scope name

reachability.summary: The attacker needs rename authority in the operator-selected scope, knowledge of a victim-readable outside target, a successful timing window, and victim indexing. OCR egress additionally requires normal online adapter approval and eligibility.
reachability.attacker: lower-trust local writer of a shared or supplied selected scope
reachability.entrypoint: non-preview `kcs index` over the selected root
preconditions: The direct child is observed as a regular file before replacement.
The attacker wins the initial check/read interval.
The outside target is readable by the KCS process.
The victim invokes indexing; OCR requires configured online execution.
reachability.outcome: one victim-readable outside file per successful replacement can cross the selected-scope boundary

impact.why: The primitive can disclose victim-readable files outside the selected scope into KCS derived/archive state, and into an OCR provider request when ordinary online controls also allow it.

likelihood.why: Exploitation requires local shared-scope rename authority, operator-mediated indexing, a known readable target, and an unmeasured race window.

limitations: Stable symlinks present before the type check are skipped.
Post-scan byte changes that do not match the scan hash are rejected.
No real target, real credential, or live provider request was used in validation.

remediation.summary: Use descriptor-bound no-follow opens for direct-child scan candidates, compute size/media/hash from the opened object, and carry verified bytes or a stable file identity through preparation and OCR instead of reopening `input_path`.
regressionTests: Replace a regular child with a symlink between scan observation and read; assert outside bytes cannot become `raw_hash` under the benign name.
Keep the replacement symlink stable through index; assert the later hash equality does not accept the outside target as an in-scope candidate.
Assert `prepare_units` consumes caller-verified bytes rather than reopening the mutable path.
Assert the OCR adapter body is built from verified bytes or a still-bound descriptor identity.
Assert stable symlinks remain skipped and ordinary regular files still index normally.
